concept.name: E2E Flake Reduction

relationships.description: Connects E2E Flake Reduction to contract testing in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Flaky end-to-end tests erode CI trust by failing non-deterministically due to async race conditions, shared mutable state, and brittle selectors—not real product bugs.
spark.keyTakeaway: Eliminate fixed `sleep()` calls in favor of web-first auto-waiting assertions, isolate per-test data and browser contexts, and track flake rate as a quantitative SLO with automated quarantine.

concept.whyItMatters: At a 2% per-test flake rate across a 100-test E2E suite, `1 - 0.98^100 = 86.7%` of CI runs fail on a completely healthy commit. Engineers start clicking 'Re-run jobs' blindly, CI queues back up, and real regressions slip into production.
whenToUse: Stabilizing critical user-journey suites (checkout, auth, billing) in Playwright or Cypress that block pull-request merges.
Diagnosing CI-only failures that pass locally on fast laptops but fail on 2-vCPU GitHub Actions or Kubernetes runners.
Building deterministic test harnesses for SPAs with heavy async hydration, WebSockets, or third-party payment iframes.
whenNotToUse: Testing fine-grained business logic, edge-case validation, or 500 error permutations that belong in fast, deterministic unit or contract tests (Test Pyramid).
Masking genuine concurrency bugs or race conditions in the application under test by adding infinite retries around broken assertions.
Scraping or load-testing production environments where E2E browser runners introduce artificial traffic spikes.
keyPoints: Never use fixed `waitForTimeout(2000)` sleeps; use web-first assertions (`await expect(locator).toBeVisible()`) that poll DOM stability and actionability.
Each test must own isolated state—create fresh users/tenants via API setup hooks and run in an isolated `BrowserContext` (clean cookies, `localStorage`, IndexedDB).
Use resilient user-facing locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`, `data-testid`) instead of auto-generated CSS classes (`.css-1x4f9`) or positional XPath (`/div[3]/button`).
Wait on explicit network or UI state transitions (`Promise.all([page.waitForResponse(...), button.click()])`) rather than assuming a click finishes synchronously.
Capture traces, DOM snapshots, and network HARs on first retry (`trace: 'on-first-retry'`) so CI failures are debuggable without reproducing locally.

examples.title: Playwright checkout hydration race condition
examples.scenario: A checkout E2E test clicked 'Pay Now' immediately after page load. On slow 2-vCPU CI runners, React had rendered the SSR button HTML before attaching the `onClick` hydration handler, causing 18% of runs to hang.
examples.outcome: Adding `await expect(payBtn).toBeEnabled()` paired with `Promise.all([page.waitForResponse(r => r.url().includes('/api/checkout') && r.status() === 200), payBtn.click()])` and deterministic API seeding dropped the flake rate from 18% to 0.1% across 500 runs.

examples.title: Shared staging user collision in parallel CI
examples.scenario: Four Playwright workers logged into the same `test@example.com` account concurrently; Test A deleted items from the cart while Test B asserted `cartCount === 2`.
examples.outcome: Replacing the shared account with a per-worker `POST /internal/test-seed` fixture returning a unique tenant ID and scoped JWT eliminated 100% of cross-test state collisions and enabled 4x parallel sharding.

tradeOffs.factor: Test retries (`retries: 2` in CI) vs strict zero-retry policy
tradeOffs.pro: Bounded retries (`retries: 1` or `2`) paired with trace capture prevent transient network blips from blocking merges while flagging `flaky` tests in telemetry.
tradeOffs.con: Unmonitored retries hide real application race conditions and double CI runner minutes on failing suites.

tradeOffs.factor: Mocked network stubs vs live backend services
tradeOffs.pro: Stubbing flaky third-party APIs (Stripe, OAuth, maps) via `page.route()` makes tests 5x faster and 100% deterministic.
tradeOffs.con: Over-mocking your own backend turns an E2E test into a frontend unit test that misses real API schema regressions.

tradeOffs.factor: Parallel worker sharding vs serial execution
tradeOffs.pro: Sharding across 4–8 workers cuts a 25-minute suite to under 4 minutes.
tradeOffs.con: Exposes every hidden shared-database or rate-limiter bottleneck immediately if test isolation is incomplete.

failureModes.name: Animation & layout-shift misclicks
failureModes.description: Clicking a modal button while a CSS slide-in transition is mid-flight causes the click coordinates to miss or hit the backdrop.
failureModes.mitigation: Disable CSS transitions in test mode (`reducedMotion: 'reduce'`) or rely on Playwright's built-in bounding-box stability check before clicks.

failureModes.name: Clock & timezone drift
failureModes.description: Tests asserting formatted dates (`Nov 12`) pass in `UTC` CI containers but fail locally in `IST` (`+05:30`) or around midnight UTC.
failureModes.mitigation: Pin `timezoneId: 'UTC'` and freeze deterministic time via `page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-11-12T10:00:00Z') })`.

failureModes.name: Third-party rate limits & CAPTCHAs
failureModes.description: CI runners sharing egress IPs trigger Auth0/Google/Stripe rate limits or bot-detection challenges after 10 parallel runs.
failureModes.mitigation: Stub third-party webhooks/widgets at the network boundary (`page.route`) and use programmatic session cookie injection for auth.

failureModes.name: Silent retry masking
failureModes.description: Tests pass on retry #2 every day, so nobody notices an underlying backend deadlock or 502 spike.
failureModes.mitigation: Export JUnit/JSON test reports to telemetry, alert when any test's flake rate exceeds 1%, and auto-quarantine chronic offenders with an assigned SLA.

commonMistakes: Using `await page.waitForTimeout(3000)` to 'fix' timing bugs, which slows the suite and still fails under CI CPU spikes.
Logging in through the UI on every single test instead of authenticating once via API (`storageState`) and reusing cookies.
Querying elements with fragile CSS chains (`div > ul > li:nth-child(2) > span`) that break on minor UI refactors.
Sharing a single seeded database row across parallel workers without unique tenant/user prefixes.
Running 300 low-value E2E tests for form field validations that belong in Vitest/Jest component tests.

sections.content:
## The idea

An E2E test is **flaky** when it passes and fails intermittently on the exact same commit without any code change. Flakiness is almost always a symptom of **non-determinism** across three boundaries: asynchronous UI/network timing, shared mutable state across tests, and environmental variance between local machines and constrained CI runners.

Reducing flakes is not about adding longer timeouts—it is about replacing time-based assumptions (`sleep(2000)`) with **event-driven synchronization** and **strict per-test isolation**.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider stabilizing a Playwright test for creating and archiving an invoice:
1. **Fast API Auth (`storageState`)**: A global setup fixture authenticates once via `POST /api/auth/login` and saves cookies/localStorage to `.auth/user.json`, cutting 3 seconds of UI login per test.
2. **Isolated Data Seed**: Before the test, a fixture calls `POST /api/test/invoices` with a unique `idempotencyKey` (`inv-${testInfo.workerIndex}-${Date.now()}`) so parallel workers never collide.
3. **Deterministic Navigation & Locators**: The test opens `/invoices/${id}` and targets `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Archive Invoice' })`.
4. **Synchronized Mutation**: It wraps the click in `Promise.all([page.waitForResponse(r => r.url().endsWith('/archive') && r.status() === 200), archiveBtn.click()])`, then asserts `await expect(page.getByText('Status: Archived')).toBeVisible()`.
5. **Forensics on Failure**: `playwright.config.ts` sets `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0` and `trace: 'on-first-retry'`, uploading the interactive DOM+network trace zip on any retry.

sections.content:
## Diagnosing CI-only flakes

When a test passes 100/100 times locally and fails 15% of the time in CI, reproduce the CI constraint locally:
- Run `npx playwright test --repeat-each=20 --workers=4` with CPU throttling (`--cpu-rate=0.25`) or inside a 2-vCPU Docker container.
- Inspect the Playwright Trace Viewer timeline for **long main-thread tasks**, **hydration gaps** (clicks firing before JS bundles execute), and **out-of-order XHR responses**.
- Audit `networkidle` usage: never rely on `waitUntil: 'networkidle'` in apps with analytics pings, polling, or WebSockets—it frequently hangs or fires prematurely.

## Anti-flake pattern reference

| Root Cause | Flaky Anti-Pattern | Deterministic Replacement | Impact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Async UI timing | `await page.waitForTimeout(2000)` | `await expect(locator).toBeVisible()` | Eliminates CPU-speed sensitivity |
| Shared state | Global `admin@test.com` user | Per-test API seed + `BrowserContext` | Enables safe parallel sharding |
| Brittle DOM | `.btn-primary >> nth=2` | `getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' })` | Survives CSS & layout refactors |
| 3rd-party API | Live Stripe / Google Maps calls | `page.route('**/stripe/**', fulfill)` | Removes external rate-limit flakes |
| Auth overhead | UI login on every `beforeEach` | API login once -> reuse `storageState` | Cuts suite runtime by 40–60% |

## Failure modes

1. **Over-retried masking**: Setting `retries: 5` turns a 20% flaky test into a 99.97% pass rate (`1 - 0.2^6`) while hiding a real backend race condition.
2. **Test-order coupling**: Test B assumes Test A created a record; sharding or running Test B standalone breaks immediately.
3. **Unbounded global teardown leaks**: Crashed tests skip `afterEach` cleanup, leaving orphaned records that slow database queries over weeks.
4. **Quarantine graveyard**: Moving flaky tests to `@quarantine` without a 7-day SLA turns quarantine into a permanent blind spot for critical user flows.

## Measuring & governing flake SLOs

Track two core metrics across your main branch:
- **Pass-on-first-try rate**: Percentage of suites passing without any retry (target `>= 98%`).
- **Test flake rate**: `(retried_and_passed) / total_runs` per test ID over a rolling 7-day window.

Automatically open a Jira/Linear ticket when any test crosses `1.5%` flake rate, and require fixes or temporary quarantine within 48 hours.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Ban `waitForTimeout` / `sleep` via ESLint rule (`playwright/no-wait-for-timeout`).
- [ ] Isolate every test with its own `BrowserContext` and unique API-seeded data.
- [ ] Replace CSS/XPath selectors with `getByRole`, `getByLabel`, or `data-testid`.
- [ ] Enable `trace: 'on-first-retry'` and `screenshot: 'only-on-failure'` in CI.
- [ ] Pin browser timezone (`UTC`), locale, and viewport dimensions (`1280x720`) across local and CI runners.
- [ ] Audit weekly flake reports and enforce a strict quarantine-fix SLA.

interviewProblems.title: E2E Flake Reduction
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on E2E Flake Reduction. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Flaky end-to-end tests erode CI trust by failing non-deterministically due to async race conditions, shared mutable state, and brittle selectors—not real product bugs.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: App + Network applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Flake Telemetry.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Flake Telemetry experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Disable CSS transitions in test mode (`reducedMotion: 'reduce'`) or rely on Playwright's built-in bounding-box stability check before clicks.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Eliminate fixed `sleep()` calls in favor of web-first auto-waiting assertions, isolate per-test data and browser contexts, and track flake rate as a quantitative SLO with automated quarantine.
Avoid trap: Using `await page.waitForTimeout(3000)` to 'fix' timing bugs, which slows the suite and still fails under CI CPU spikes.
Avoid trap: Logging in through the UI on every single test instead of authenticating once via API (`storageState`) and reusing cookies.
When to reach for it: Stabilizing critical user-journey suites (checkout, auth, billing) in Playwright or Cypress that block pull-request merges.
When to reach for it: Diagnosing CI-only failures that pass locally on fast laptops but fail on 2-vCPU GitHub Actions or Kubernetes runners.

putItTogether.title: Putting E2E Flake Reduction Together
putItTogether.summary: Eliminate fixed `sleep()` calls in favor of web-first auto-waiting assertions, isolate per-test data and browser contexts, and track flake rate as a quantitative SLO with automated quarantine.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for E2E Flake Reduction before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Adding `await expect(payBtn).toBeEnabled()` paired with `Promise.all([page.waitForResponse(r => r.url().includes('/api/checkout') && r.status() === 200), payBtn.click()])` and deterministic API seeding dropped the flake rate from 18% to 0.1% across 500 runs.
